bug_semantics: LocalFolderExtractor derives an output File directly from an attacker-controlled RAR entry name and compares canonical path strings with startsWith(destinationCanonicalPath). For destination /tmp/extract, an entry ../extract_evil/pwned.txt canonicalizes to /tmp/extract_evil/pwned.txt, which still starts with the string /tmp/extract; the guard therefore accepts a sibling path and FileOutputStream writes attacker-controlled archive content outside the extraction directory.
flaw_origin: The unsafe extraction lineage is older than the repository's Git history: root commit 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519 is an 'initial import' that already constructs a destination File from the archive header name without containment validation in testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java. The code was subsequently moved into Junrar.java by 75cb6a58c9b3ca08db954eec241b91a5331dd632 and into LocalFolderExtractor.java by 3b645d991563dd8933f6efab135cd76a43a92d6b. Commit e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a later attempted to stop traversal with the defective canonical-string prefix check, preserving the sibling-prefix exploit until the 7.5.10 fix.
ai_marker: unavailable: the true smallest BIC predates the public Git history, so no BIC commit object exists to inspect. The boundary object 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519 is a root 'initial import' authored and committed by Edmund Wagner <edmund-wagner@web.de> with no trailers, but that aggregate import is not substituted for the unavailable original BIC and cannot establish its AI attribution.
evidence: The reviewed GitHub advisory API endpoints https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-HF5P-Q87M-CRJ7 and https://api.github.com/repos/junrar/junrar/security-advisories/GHSA-hf5p-q87m-crj7 identify com.github.junrar:junrar <7.5.10, first patched 7.5.10, and describe the /tmp/extract versus /tmp/extract_evil sibling-prefix bypass in LocalFolderExtractor.createDirectory/createFile. git diff a60857b35c17dbd5354a37816421d7b051a8ba03 d77e9a83eb721cd51f9c23d7869d0e6ad7f952d7 shows the direct fix appending File.separator to both canonical destination prefixes and adding sibling-prefix-traversal.rar plus a regression test expecting /tmp/extract_evil/pwned.txt to be rejected. git tag --contains d77e9a83eb721cd51f9c23d7869d0e6ad7f952d7 lists v7.5.10 and later but not v7.5.9, matching the patched boundary. git log -S'new File(destination, name)' --all --reverse -- . reaches only root 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519; git rev-list --max-parents=0 --all confirms it is the sole parentless root. That root's testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java:104 accepts the archive-derived name in new File(destination, name), and its extraction loop opens FileOutputStream on that result without any containment check. The root commit object says only 'initial import', and therefore provides no earlier parent tree or original authoring commit to test. History reconstruction excludes non-BIC transformations: 75cb6a58c9b3ca08db954eec241b91a5331dd632 copied the extraction implementation from ExtractArchive into Junrar, 3b645d991563dd8933f6efab135cd76a43a92d6b moved it into LocalFolderExtractor, and e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a added the incomplete startsWith canonical-path guard. git tag --no-contains e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a includes vulnerable com.github.junrar release junrar-3.1.0, proving e60 is an attempted partial fix rather than the lifecycle BIC. The fix reference is https://github.com/junrar/junrar/commit/d77e9a83eb721cd51f9c23d7869d0e6ad7f952d7 and the release reference is https://github.com/junrar/junrar/releases/tag/v7.5.10.
reasoning: The attacker-controlled RAR header name flows through createFile to FileOutputStream. Before 2019 the lineage had no containment check at all; e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a added canonicalization but used a lexical prefix without a separator boundary, so ordinary ../ traversal was narrowed while the sibling-name-prefix form remained exploitable. The 2026 direct fix d77e9a83eb721cd51f9c23d7869d0e6ad7f952d7 changes both guards to destinationCanonicalPath + File.separator, causing the crafted sibling canonical path to fail, and it first appears in v7.5.10. The earliest public Git object already contains the unsafe archive-name-to-filesystem sink and is explicitly an aggregate initial import with no parent; later copies, moves, and the incomplete guard cannot be called the smallest BIC. Because there is no immediate parent tree for the imported code, introducer_parent is null and introducer_parent_absent remains false rather than claiming a comparison that cannot exist. The true authoring commit and its commit-object AI marker are outside reachable public history, which is a genuine public-history boundary and therefore BLOCKED rather than NOT_AI or EVIDENCE_GAP.
remaining_gap: The original pre-import source-control commit that first wrote the archive-entry-name-to-output-file mechanism, its immediate parent tree, and that true BIC's commit-object author/committer/trailers are unavailable from the public repository; the sole Git root is already an aggregate initial import containing the flaw.
